qa.answer: Four options. Issue the 45 kits from free stock and move three overdue consumable lines (saves USD 1.5K, no slip, recommended), buy the kits from Seletar Engine Parts (USD 27K, no slip), re-sequence WO-2617 so the leads fit at final assembly (no cost, medium risk if the closure is extended), or accept a 2 day slip and pay Tanjong Pacific USD 24K in LDs.

The recommended option is the cheapest: issuing from stock costs nothing, and Klang penetrant at USD 54 and Rheinland masking tape at USD 299 save USD 3.2K, against a USD 1.7K premium on Jurong solvent wipes. Net it saves USD 1,468. The cheapest option that buys new kits is the Seletar distributor buy at USD 27K.

In 2022 a health closure shut a harness plant for four weeks (PRE-11); we bought from a distributor for the first two engines and repaired serviceable leads for the rest, for USD 31K and 2 days of slip, and every engine redelivered on time. This time free stock covers WO-2617, which matches the 2024 seal batch case (PRE-09): reallocating released stock of the same part is the fastest lever. Keep the PRE-11 repair route in reserve if the closure runs past three weeks.

WO-2617 needs 45 ignition lead harness kits at induction on 26 Oct, and the scoring ties them to PO line 4500018722-00010, which the closure moves to 3 Nov. That is an 8 day slip against 6 days of float, so Tanjong Pacific's redelivery moves 2 days to 2 Jan. The scoring does not net free stock, which is why issuing from INV-0029 removes the move entirely.
